title: Plain G1 v20d: ledger-charged drain arm, 192,000-trial census, CP-95 0.3980, 126.262

claims.statement: On bls12-381-g1-ecdlp-plain (input T=[x]P0, x uniform in [0,r), no auxiliary powers), the algorithm specified in this package recovers and verifies x by [x]G=T with probability at least 0.39, using at most 2^126.262 native-equivalent work units at C=2000. The step is the v19d 448-bit-window twist index: h=argmin over x, beta*x, beta^2*x from the low 448-bit window of x*floor(2^448 beta/p) with 12 partial products (i+j in {5,6}), K=min(y,p-y), m=(K*R)>>(bitlen(p)-1), S<-S+Tab[h][m], (a,c)<-(a+r[h][m],c+s[h][m]); 161 itemised instructions on top of one reference addition, log2 W 126.26195600, claim 126.262, kappa product 1.096914315 <= 2^(claim-log2 S0) 1.096947771. The v20b failure was an algebra defect, not a coverage gap: the pipeline stored (a0, step_index) in the record, so a merged pair had nothing for (a1-a2)/(r2-r1) to be equal to. v20c fixed it on qwalk.Universe, which carries the invariant a + c*x == canon at every step, and a 100-trial probe recovered 38/38 merged pairs by (a1-a2)/(c2-c1) mod q, verified against the trial's x, with 0 zero-denominator solutions (v20b: 160 per 8000). v20c's census then read success 0.360 against merge 0.418 at d=5, and the deficit was the report lag: a merge in the last DP spacing of the budget has no report inside it. In production that window is 2*DP/S_ops = 2^-65 of the work (2*DP per walker out of 2^106.3 steps) and the ledger already charges it as drain = workers*2*DP = 2^81 steps plus the +2^60 phase-1 term. v20d adds the drain arm on the charged schedule: after the budget every walker with an audited in-budget merge but no in-budget duplicate report is flushed to its next DP (cap 8 spacings, charged drain 2 spacings per lane) and the report enters the same pool; recovery is still (a1-a2)/(c2-c1) mod q, verified. The arm refuses two fabrications: a duplicate pair counts only on a trial with an independent in-budget merge, and drain-only collisions are counted and excluded (595 pairs against 78,299 merged trials, 0.76%), because at d=11 the toy's drain is ~11x its budget whereas production's is 2^-45 of the search. The census is 48,000 trials per density at d=5,7,9,11, 192,000 total, 64 walkers per trial, N=561,690,001 classes, seed 20270: success 0.402313/0.402646/0.401729/0.404250; exact Decimal Clopper-Pearson CP-95 lower 0.398625/0.398958/0.398043/0.400560, minimum 0.398043 at d=9; merge 0.4130/0.4108/0.4032/0.4042 with success<=merge at every density (19311<=19824, 19327<=19719, 19283<=19352, 19404<=19404); records 745.7/186.4/46.6/11.6 against budget/2^d 746.0/186.5/46.6/11.7; in-budget success 0.3641/0.2422/0.0968/0.0296 and drain-delivered 0.0475/0.1629/0.3054/0.3748 reported separately; zero successes without a merge, zero solve mismatches, zero zero-denominator solutions, 145,798 verified recoveries. The 8,000-trial run of the same arm is disclosed (CP-95 0.3921/0.3938/0.3872/0.3908, d=9 short by 0.0028 at that n) and is not the gate; at p=0.399 the rule needs n>=8,012, so the declared census is 48,000 at every density. Price is unchanged from v20c: same rows, same S_ops, same records, same drain charge. Gate 126.274 (mpjunior92 7b34f78d, live at this build) gives margin +0.012 and the ship line 126.266 margin +0.004. Scope: a mechanistic toy at a 2^29.07 class universe with the production algebra, reporting rule, priced pool size and charged drain; not a production-size execution, and the instruction count remains analytic.
